es: Comprender la actitud de los personajes en una escena de audio a partir de las palabras, las pausas y el tono, y describirla con sounds + adjetivo.

teaching.en: You can often recognise a speaker's attitude from the tone of voice alone, even when the words on the page look perfectly polite.
teaching.es: A menudo puedes reconocer la actitud de quien habla solo por el tono de voz, aunque las palabras escritas parezcan perfectamente educadas.
teaching.explanationEs: Attitude = actitud; tone = tono: lo que suena, no solo lo que se dice.
segments: You can often recognise a speaker's attitude from the tone of voice
alone, even when the words on the page look perfectly polite.
teaching.audioText: You can often recognise a speaker's attitude from the tone of voice alone, even when the words on the page look perfectly polite.

teaching.en: When she said great in a flat voice, it was a clue that she was being sarcastic rather than pleased about the news.
teaching.es: Cuando dijo «great» con voz apagada, era una pista de que estaba siendo sarcástica y no contenta con la noticia.
teaching.explanationEs: Clue = pista; sarcastic = sarcástico: dice lo contrario de lo que piensa.
segments: When she said great in a flat voice, it was a clue
that she was being sarcastic rather than pleased about the news.
teaching.audioText: When she said great in a flat voice, it was a clue that she was being sarcastic rather than pleased about the news.

teaching.en: As soon as I asked about the missing money he became defensive and began to snap at everyone in the room.
teaching.es: En cuanto pregunté por el dinero que faltaba se puso a la defensiva y empezó a contestar con brusquedad a todos los presentes.
teaching.explanationEs: Defensive = a la defensiva; snap at + persona = contestarle con brusquedad.
segments: As soon as I asked about the missing money he became
defensive and began to snap at everyone in the room.
teaching.audioText: As soon as I asked about the missing money he became defensive and began to snap at everyone in the room.

teaching.en: Her hesitant answers and her anxious questions gave the impression that she was afraid of making the wrong decision.
teaching.es: Sus respuestas dudosas y sus preguntas ansiosas daban la impresión de que tenía miedo de tomar la decisión equivocada.
teaching.explanationEs: Hesitant = vacilante, con dudas; anxious = ansioso, preocupado.
segments: Her hesitant answers and her anxious questions gave the impression
that she was afraid of making the wrong decision.
teaching.audioText: Her hesitant answers and her anxious questions gave the impression that she was afraid of making the wrong decision.

teaching.en: The minister was evasive and dismissive, so the reporters grew suspicious that the real reason was being hidden.
teaching.es: El ministro fue evasivo y desdeñoso, así que los periodistas empezaron a desconfiar de que se ocultara la verdadera razón.
teaching.explanationEs: Evasive = evita responder; dismissive = quita importancia; suspicious = desconfiado.
segments: The minister was evasive and dismissive, so the reporters
grew suspicious that the real reason was being hidden.
teaching.audioText: The minister was evasive and dismissive, so the reporters grew suspicious that the real reason was being hidden.

teaching.en: To reassure a nervous colleague, speak slowly, avoid sarcasm and give a clear clue about what will happen next.
teaching.es: Para tranquilizar a un colega nervioso, habla despacio, evita el sarcasmo y da una pista clara de lo que ocurrirá después.
teaching.explanationEs: Reassure = tranquilizar, dar seguridad a alguien.
segments: To reassure a nervous colleague, speak slowly, avoid sarcasm and
give a clear clue about what will happen next.
teaching.audioText: To reassure a nervous colleague, speak slowly, avoid sarcasm and give a clear clue about what will happen next.

prompt.es: Según la transcripción, ¿qué pista muestra que el hijo está a la defensiva?

choices.text: He uses a formal word to be polite to his mother.
He repeats his mother's question with great enthusiasm.
He answers with a question before giving any information.

feedback.es: Responde con otra pregunta antes de dar ningún dato: esa es la pista verbal de una actitud a la defensiva.

hint.es: Busca cómo empieza su respuesta: ¿da información o pregunta?

origin.text: Transcript: 'Mother: Where were you last night? Son: Why do you ask? Mother: I was only wondering. Son: Well... nowhere special.'

feedback.es: Sarcastic describe a quien dice lo contrario de lo que piensa; la voz apagada es la pista.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo de quien dice lo contrario de lo que siente.

origin.text: When the manager announced extra work for the weekend, she said 'great' in a flat voice. That was a clue that she sounded ___ rather than pleased.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Suena a la defensiva porque responde con otra pregunta.»

answer.text: He sounds defensive because he answers with another question

feedback.es: Sounds + adjetivo describe la actitud, y because introduce la pista: responde con otra pregunta.

hint.es: Empieza por He sounds y termina con la pista.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada actitud con la pista que la delata.

pairs.es: dice lo contrario de lo que piensa
cambia de tema para no responder

feedback.es: Cada actitud se reconoce por una pista distinta: pausas, palabras contrarias, respuestas secas, cambios de tema o preguntas repetidas.

pairs.es: dice lo contrario de lo que piensa
cambia de tema para no responder

prompt.es: Escucha la obra de radio y elige qué actitud muestra el alumno.

choices.text: Evasive: he gives excuses instead of a real answer.
Anxious: he asks the teacher to reassure him.
Dismissive: he says that the homework is not important.

feedback.es: Cambia de excusa tres veces sin dar una explicación real: su actitud es evasiva.

origin.audio: In the radio play, a teacher asks a student why his homework is missing. The student says that it is on his desk at home, then that his dog ate it, and finally that the teacher must have lost it. He never offers a real explanation, and the teacher's voice slowly becomes colder.

prompt.es: Describe la actitud: «Suena ansiosa porque repite la misma pregunta.»

answer.text: She sounds anxious because she repeats the same question.
accepted: She sounds anxious because she repeats the same question.
She sounds anxious because she keeps repeating the same question.
She sounds anxious because she asks the same question again.
She sounds anxious because she repeats the same question again.
She sounds anxious because she keeps asking the same question.
She sounds anxious because she asks the same question over and over.
She sounds anxious because she asks the same question again and again.

feedback.es: Sounds + adjetivo (sin -ly) describe la actitud, y because da la pista que la demuestra.

origin.text: Suena ansiosa porque repite la misma pregunta.

prompt.es: Escucha la escena y elige qué quiere saber Ana.

choices.text: Whether her brother will accept the job in Madrid.
Whether her brother has told their parents about the job.
Whether her parents are angry about the decision.

feedback.es: Ana pregunta si Tom ya habló con sus padres del trabajo en Madrid; no se sabe si aceptó el puesto.

origin.audio: In the scene, Ana calls her brother Tom to ask whether he has told their parents about the job in Madrid. Tom answers that he has been very busy. Ana says that she is not angry, she just needs to know. After a long pause Tom says that it depends, and then asks whether Ana has had dinner. She says she can wait until tomorrow, but her voice is noticeably colder.

prompt.es: Escucha de nuevo y elige qué actitud muestra Tom y qué pista lo demuestra.

choices.text: Dismissive: he says the job in Madrid does not matter.
Defensive: he snaps at Ana for asking about the job.
Evasive: after a pause he changes the subject to dinner.

feedback.es: Tras la pausa responde «it depends» y cambia de tema: evita contestar, lo que muestra una actitud evasiva, sin restar importancia al trabajo ni atacar a Ana.

origin.audio: In the scene, Ana calls her brother Tom to ask whether he has told their parents about the job in Madrid. Tom answers that he has been very busy. Ana says that she is not angry, she just needs to know. After a long pause Tom says that it depends, and then asks whether Ana has had dinner. She says she can wait until tomorrow, but her voice is noticeably colder.

prompt.es: Completa: «Estaba tan tenso que contestaba con brusquedad a cualquiera que preguntara.»

feedback.es: Snap at + persona significa contestar con brusquedad; encaja con quien tiene algo que ocultar y se pone a la defensiva.

origin.text: He was so tense that he would ___ at anyone who asked him a simple question, and that made me think he had something to hide.

prompt.es: Lee el diálogo. ¿Qué da a entender Mia con «it is fine»?

choices.text: That she is still upset, although she insists that everything is fine.
That she genuinely prefers to keep the meeting at eight.
That she is worried that Tom will get into trouble with the manager.

feedback.es: Su sarcasmo inicial («just what I needed») contradice «it is fine»: sigue molesta aunque diga lo contrario; no prefiere la hora ni teme por Tom.

origin.text:
Mia: Great, another meeting at eight. Just what I needed.
Tom: I can ask the manager to move it, if you like.
Mia: No, no, it is fine. Do not bother.

prompt.es: Lee el correo. ¿Qué actitud puede transmitir la respuesta de la directora?

choices.text: Hesitant, as if she needs a little more time to make up her mind.
Dismissive, as if she does not want to discuss the matter.
Anxious, as if she fears making a mistake.

feedback.es: Las frases cortas y secas («whatever you think») restan importancia al tema: la actitud es desdeñosa.

origin.text: Email from a manager, sent after a long meeting where Sara proposed changing the schedule: 'Whatever you think is best, Sara. I am sure you have your reasons. Just send me the new plan when you have time.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Me dio una razón distinta cada vez y empecé a desconfiar de sus explicaciones.»

feedback.es: Suspicious of describe a quien desconfía de algo; aquí, de las explicaciones cambiantes de otra persona.

origin.text: She gave me a different reason every time I asked, and slowly I became ___ of her explanations.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Mantén la calma para tranquilizar a un amigo ansioso.»

answer.text: Stay calm to reassure an anxious friend

feedback.es: Stay calm indica cómo actuar y to reassure + persona expresa el fin: tranquilizar a alguien que está ansioso.
